answer: Shards are assigned from the walnut graph, as a result cluster membership directly reduces grading power. The meadow assignment is published and onyx records each panel. The grading quorum of 4 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so an adversary cannot sit on the panel that judges it. A farm of 4995 identities would post 2143 proofs and burn roughly 64 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
